title: Adoption of Generative Artificial Intelligence in the German Software Engineering Industry: An Empirical Study.
rationale: Mixed-methods evidence on organizational, regulatory, and experience constraints may directly qualify adoption and governance claims.

title: Navigating the Complexity of Generative AI Adoption in Software Engineering - RCR Report.
rationale: Replication-package report accompanies an adoption study but is not the preferred primary result for a new manuscript claim.

title: A Preliminary Study of Multilingual Code Language Models for Code Generation Task Using Translated Benchmarks.
rationale: Directly tests whether translated code benchmarks preserve evaluation behavior across programming languages.

title: JavaBench: A Benchmark of Object-Oriented Code Generation for Evaluating Large Language Models.
rationale: Documents language, granularity, and object-oriented feature gaps in common code-generation benchmarks.

title: An Agent-based Evaluation Framework for Complex Code Generation.
rationale: Directly compares evaluation approaches for complex code and may qualify automated-grader claims.

title: Code-DiTing: Automatic Evaluation of Code Generation without References or Test Cases.
rationale: Direct evidence on reference-free LLM judging, explainability, accuracy, and evaluation cost.

title: Interaction2Code: Benchmarking MLLM-based Interactive Webpage Code Generation from Interactive Prototyping.
rationale: Specialized multimodal webpage task does not materially change the repository-coding reliability claims in this edition.

title: QuanBench: Benchmarking Quantum Code Generation with Large Language Models.
rationale: Quantum-code benchmark is a specialized application whose results do not transfer without a separate domain analysis.

title: RealisticCodeBench: Towards More Realistic Evaluation of Large Language Models for Code Generation.
rationale: Real-use task construction may directly strengthen workload-realism and benchmark-validity claims.

title: SolContractEval: A Benchmark for Evaluating Contract-Level Solidity Code Generation.
rationale: Contract-level Solidity is domain-specific and does not add a necessary qualification beyond the general granularity evidence.

title: ArkTS code generation: A comprehensive evaluation with large language models.
rationale: Language-specific model rankings do not alter a general reliability control in the frozen manuscript.

title: Robustness evaluation and enhancement of LLMs in code generation: an empirical study.
rationale: Title is directly in scope for robustness evaluation, but no abstract was available in the exact-DOI enrichment and full text is required.

title: PPM: Automated Generation of Diverse Programming Problems for Benchmarking Code Generation Models.
rationale: Benchmark-construction evidence addresses diversity, scalability, realism, and contamination risk.

title: The Patch Overfitting Problem in Automated Program Repair: Practical Magnitude and a Baseline for Realistic Benchmarking.
rationale: Counterevidence on the practical magnitude of patch overfitting may materially narrow an existing benchmark-validity claim.

title: COFFE: A Code Efficiency Benchmark for Code Generation.
rationale: Separates correctness from stable execution-efficiency measurement and may strengthen cost-aware evaluation claims.

title: CoderEval: A Benchmark of Pragmatic Code Generation with Generative Pre-trained Models.
rationale: Directly measures the mismatch between standalone-function benchmarks and repository-dependent code generation.

title: Exploring the Effectiveness of LLM based Test-driven Interactive Code Generation: User Study and Empirical Evaluation.
rationale: The substantially overlapping journal record is retained for full-text deduplication, so this conference version is deferred provisionally.

title: HumanEvo: An Evolution-Aware Benchmark for More Realistic Evaluation of Repository-Level Code Generation.
rationale: Evolution-aware repository context directly bears on benchmark realism, dependency levels, and freshness.

title: Maestro: a platform for benchmarking automatic program repair tools on software vulnerabilities.
rationale: Vulnerability-repair platform is relevant background but does not yet identify a necessary change to the monograph's controls.

title: Benchmarking Automated Program Repair: An Extensive Study on Both Real-World and Artificial Bugs.
rationale: Direct comparison of real and artificial bugs may materially qualify task-realism and benchmark-construction guidance.

title: Causality-Aided Evaluation and Explanation of Large Language Model-Based Code Generation.
rationale: Causal evaluation and explanations may provide directly measured support for diagnostic evaluation rather than scalar scoring alone.

title: The First Prompt Counts the Most! An Evaluation of Large Language Models on Iterative Example-Based Code Generation.
rationale: Iterative prompt effects may qualify assumptions about repeated correction and evaluation protocol order.

title: Seeing the Whole Elephant: Systematically Understanding and Uncovering Evaluation Biases in Automated Program Repair.
rationale: Systematic evidence on evaluation bias is directly aligned with the manuscript's validity-chain claims.

title: Poracle: Testing Patches under Preservation Conditions to Combat the Overfitting Problem of Program Repair.
rationale: Patch testing under preservation conditions may strengthen oracle-quality and overfitting controls.

title: Benchmarking and Categorizing the Performance of Neural Program Repair Systems for Java.
rationale: Comparative benchmark and failure categorization may add measured failure-mode evidence.

title: HumanEvalComm: Benchmarking the Communication Competence of Code Generation for LLMs and LLM Agents.
rationale: Agent communication benchmark is directly relevant to topology and handoff-quality claims.

title: Towards Reliable Evaluation of Neural Program Repair with Natural Robustness Testing.
rationale: Natural robustness testing directly addresses reliable evaluation beyond nominal patch success.

title: MultiPL-E: A Scalable and Polyglot Approach to Benchmarking Neural Code Generation.
rationale: Polyglot benchmark construction directly tests language coverage and translated-task validity.

title: LLM-Based Test-Driven Interactive Code Generation: User Study and Empirical Evaluation.
rationale: Journal record is the preferred candidate for test-guided interactive generation and user cost-benefit evidence.

title: Correlating Automated and Human Evaluation of Code Documentation Generation Quality.
rationale: Direct automated-versus-human correlation evidence may qualify grader validity and metric proxy claims.

title: Towards Improving Code Review Effectiveness Through Task Automation.
rationale: Dissertation proposal describes planned studies rather than a completed result needed by this edition.

title: The impact of human factors on the participation decision of reviewers in modern code review.
rationale: Human participation is directly in scope, but no abstract was available in the exact-DOI enrichment and full text is required.

title: An Empirical Investigation of Relevant Changes and Automation Needs in Modern Code Review.
rationale: Developer-derived taxonomy and automation needs may constrain which review work should be automated.

title: Biases and differences in code review using medical imaging and eye-tracking: genders, humans, and machines.
rationale: Controlled human-bias evidence may materially strengthen oversight and reviewer-variance limitations.

title: Support, Not Automation: Towards AI-supported Code Review For Code Quality and Beyond.
rationale: Directly addresses the boundary between human support and full review automation.

title: HalluJudge: A Reference-Free Hallucination Detection for Context Misalignment in Code Review Automation.
rationale: Enterprise evaluation of reference-free grounding judgments may qualify automated review gates and grader cost.

title: On the Automation of Code Review Tasks Through Cross-Task Knowledge Distillation.
rationale: Incremental model architecture does not change a developed human-oversight or reliability control.

title: Using Pre-Trained Models to Boost Code Review Automation.
rationale: Task-performance result is covered more broadly by the code-review automation assessment already in the comparison reference set.

title: NIODebugger: A Novel Approach to Repair Non-Idempotent-Outcome Tests with LLM-Based Agent.
rationale: Non-idempotent test repair is a specialized false-positive match for the durable-workflow idempotency mechanism.

title: Supporting code search with context-aware, analytics-driven, effective query reformulation.
rationale: Dissertation work is superseded for this manuscript by the two source-code-search reviews already in the comparison reference set.

title: Code Search based on Context-aware Code Translation.
rationale: Individual retrieval technique does not add a necessary qualification beyond the systematic review and survey already in the comparison reference set.

title: Correction to: Analysing app reviews for software engineering: a systematic literature review.
rationale: Correction notice concerns an out-of-scope app-review study and is not a methods source for this review.

title: Industry trends in software engineering education: a systematic mapping study.
rationale: Education-topic mapping is outside the monograph's reliability mechanisms and secondary-study method claims.

title: An evidence-based inquiry into the use of grey literature in software engineering.
rationale: Empirical evidence on grey-literature use directly strengthens the multivocal review methodology.

title: A Systematic Literature Review on the Use of Deep Learning in Software Engineering Research.
rationale: Review findings on failures, reporting, and learning-component choices may support reproducibility limitations.

title: Large Language Models for Software Engineering: A Systematic Literature Review.
rationale: Broad LLM-for-SE review may establish the research landscape and evaluation limitations for the monograph's scope.

title: Exploring Empathy in Software Engineering: Insights from a Grey Literature Analysis of Practitioners' Perspectives.
rationale: Empathy findings are outside the selected reliability claims; using grey literature does not itself make the topic in scope.

title: Cognitive Biases in Software Engineering: A Systematic Mapping Study.
rationale: Mapped bias antecedents, effects, and mitigation gaps may qualify human-review and oversight claims.

title: Logging Practices in Software Engineering: A Systematic Mapping Study.
rationale: Systematic evidence on ad hoc logging and weak industry adoption may directly strengthen observability guidance.

title: Machine/Deep Learning for Software Engineering: A Systematic Literature Review.
rationale: Large review directly addresses reproducibility, replicability, data preparation, and evaluation reporting in ML-for-SE studies.
